description: Here at The Exploration Company, we are building spacecraft for humanity. Here at The Exploration Company, we are developing, producing, and operating Nyx, a modular and reusable space orbital vehicle that can eventually be refuelled in orbit, and which carries cargo – and potentially humans in the long run. We are also developing different types of propulsion systems to power our future vehicles and missions. As a talented Test Development Engineer , you will be part of the team that is responsible for the development of test facilities for our future propulsion systems. Key Responsibilities / Tasks: In your capacity as a Test Development Engineer , your role will be continuously evolving, but day to day your duties may include: Synthesise test bench requirements from user and operator needs and plan required verification methods and tests. Translate engine test objectives and stakeholder needs into facility-level functional and performance requirements. Perform technical trade-offs to determine the best choice of hardware, software, equipment, component, location etc for various test facilities. Perform risk assessment analyses for future tests and developing mitigation actions to ensure personnel and hardware safety. Provide technical inputs to cost, schedule, procurement, commissioning, maintainability, and facility acceptance planning. Prepare and maintain P&IDs of test facilities based on test bench requirements and selecting components. Undertaking preliminary design of the ground support equipment with minimal oversight. Undertake hazard assessments of the test facility design (FMEA and HAZOPs) to determine if any additional changes to the design are required. Work with the current test bench team to coordinate end-to-end activities of the development of test facilities including design, reviews, manufacturing, installation, commissioning, test operations, ongoing upgrades and maintenance. Work with procurement, AIT and design teams during the development of test facilities to find the right balance of technical solutions, cost and lead time. Presenting findings to team members and participating in design reviews and project discussions. What we would love to see from you: Bachelor's, master's or PhD in aerospace engineering, mechanical engineering, or a related field (Master’s and above preferred). 2–5 years of experience in propulsion, test facility development, experimental engineering, or a related field. Practical experience in the design, development, commissioning, or operation of test facilities, preferably for rocket propulsion systems. Experience in test facility design for cryogenic propulsion systems is highly desirable. Relevant experience with other cryogenic or high-pressure fluid systems will also be considered. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret technical data, challenge assumptions, and make evidence-based engineering recommendations. Proven ability to work autonomously on assigned technical topics while contributing effectively to a multidisciplinary engineering team. Excellent communication and leadership skills, with the ability to convey complex concepts to diverse audiences. Why you should join us! What makes us special here at The Exploration Company and why we think you will enjoy working here is: We’re Agile - we make decisions fast whilst keeping our goals and systems in mind We’re Open and Collaborative - we are transparent about risks and obstacles, so that we can cooperate to overcome them We have a lot of Fun - we refuel our energy knowing we are democratising space. It’s a wonderful and rare opportunity, are YOU up for the challenge? We'd love to hear from you if you wish to be a part of our journey. Please submit your CV now for immediate consideration and we will be in touch shortly. The Exploration Company is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status or disability status. Relocation assistance is provided for those willing to relocate including visa sponsorship where applicable. All offers are contingent upon the successful completion of a background check, which will be subject to the country, role, and project you applied for. By submitting your application, you acknowledge and agree that any offer of employment may be conditional upon successful condition of this check. The Exploration Company partners with Zinc Work Limited located in the UK (Zinc), a third-party provider, to ensure this process as efficient and transparent as possible. If applicable, you will receive an email from Zinc upon acceptance of your offer with a link to a secure portal where you can provide the required information to Zinc. description:
In a nutshell

At Picnic, we're building the most secure milkman on earth. Our Security team owns the security tooling that protects Picnic, and we're looking for a Java Engineer to make it work everywhere: connecting our systems to those tools, automating checks across the whole company, and strengthening how we manage identity and access.
You'll be the engineer in the Security team. Instead of writing policies, you'll write the code that wires our security systems into the rest of Picnic, and you'll help product teams do the right thing by default.

Tricks of the trade

  • Ownership: Take ownership of projects from concept to delivery, aligning technical solutions with business goals with a product engineering mindset.
  • Platform work: Own Picnic’s core Security and IAM platform services, and build integrations with internal and external services.
  • Identity & Access: Help take our IAM initiative from MVP to production. Look at the options, build or integrate the pieces and connect them to the systems Picnic runs on.
  • Collaboration: Work closely with development teams to integrate security best practices into the software development lifecycle.
  • Security Ambassador: Conduct application security workshops to raise awareness and promote secure coding practices among developers.
  • Our Tech: Java 21/25 (Spring 6 with Spring Boot 3.5, Reactor, Immutables, Maven), React, Angular, RabbitMQ, Kafka, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Git, Docker, AWS, Helm, Terraform, Kubernetes, Vault, Datadog, Python 3.x

We’re looking for

  • You have a Master’s Degree (in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Information Technology, Computer Engineering or a related technical field) or equivalent experience.
  • You have at least 3-7 years of professional experience with Java.
  • A genuine curiosity about security: experience isn’t required, but you’re excited to dive into topics like access control and to grow into the domain with us.
  • Your English skills are on point (no Dutch required).
  • You're based in or happy to relocate to the Netherlands*

    For bonus points:
  • Experience with Security frameworks like NIST, CIS Controls
  • Working experience in IAM integrations

We work from our office in Amsterdam. Being present makes a genuine difference to your team and the work. There's flexibility to work from home when needed, but if remote or hybrid-first is what you're after, this probably isn't the right fit.

Picnic Perks

✍🏼 Every expert was once a beginner!

You’ll get plenty of opportunities to challenge yourself and grow, including the Picnic Tech Academy, Lunch & Learn sessions, and tailored soft skills training. We also offer free professional weekly language courses.

💡 Make a difference

You’ll work in an awesome startup environment with the freedom to drive your own projects and create a visible impact. Our fully electric vehicles and sustainable business model mean you’ll also be contributing to making the world a better place!

🫱🏼‍🫲🏾 Teamwork makes the dream work

With more than 80 nationalities across 3 countries, you’ll be part of a diverse company with plenty of cool stuff to get involved with, from board game evenings to after-work drinks to our company ski trip and more!

🍎 You are what you eat

You’ll get freshly prepared, healthy lunches and snacks (with plenty of vegetarian, vegan, and halal options). Coffee snob? Don’t worry, our amazing Picnic barista has you covered.

🚴🏽 Stay healthy

Mental health is important. As well as having the option to speak with Picnic colleagues who act as confidential advisors, our collaboration with OpenUp gives you easy access to professional psychologists, along with workshops and materials. There are plenty of sports communities and events to get involved with, from tennis to yoga, to climbing!

🔋 Attractive package

We offer competitive compensation and a pension plan that looks out for your future self, as well as 25 vacation days per year, so you can recharge your batteries

🌍 Benefits for expats

It can be daunting starting a new job AND moving to a new country. That’s why we offer lots of support for our many expat colleagues, if you want to find our relocation benefits, see here.

description: About Mistral Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. The mission You will be the reference point for the most complex hardware interventions across our sites. Mistral's compute is our largest investment and the foundation of frontier AI in Europe. As a Senior Data Center Hardware Engineer , you own the interventions that require the highest level of technical expertise: multi-node failures in production, full-rack deployments of GPU-dense systems, and vendor escalations where you speak as the technical authority for our sites. You'll work end-to-end — compute, storage, interconnect, power and cooling interfaces — across our data center footprint, raising the bar on reliability as our capacity grows. This is a hands-on senior IC role: deep technical leadership and mentorship, no direct line management. Location: Based at one of our data centers in the Paris region, with occasional visits to our other sites as needed. What you'll do Lead complex interventions — vendor-level and multi-node operations in production: full rack builds and bring-up, GPU-dense platform deployment (H100/H200-class and next-gen, including liquid-cooled racks), intricate recabling, post-restart diagnosis. You own the plan, the risk assessment, and the rollback. Own vendor management — coordinate repairs, part replacements and escalations directly with hardware vendors; hold them to their SLAs; drive proactive fixes from failure trends. Diagnose at depth — correlate symptoms across compute, storage, interconnect and cooling; read BMC/IPMI consoles, OS logs and crash dumps; methodical root-cause analysis that ends in concrete corrective actions. Deploy and validate — structured bring-up and validation of new racks and platforms; work with networking and infrastructure teams to take installations from delivery to production-ready. Lift the team — mentor and pair with L1–L3 engineers on live operations; turn your knowledge into SOPs, checklists and training material; propose and build small automation (Python/Bash) to shorten MTTR. Work the facility interface — partner with critical facilities/engineering ops on power, cooling (air and liquid), PDU and monitoring (BMS/EPMS) boundaries; enforce ESD/LOTO/PPE and audit-ready change discipline everywhere. Own spares & reliability — plan spares strategy, track fleet failure trends, and run proactive vendor actions before incidents happen. About you 6+ years in data center / server hardware or L2/L3 hardware support, including complex hands-on work in production environments (HPC/AI/cloud at scale strongly preferred). End-to-end hardware expertise: CPU/memory/PCIe (incl. accelerators), NICs, PSUs, drives, network, power and cooling interfaces (DLC included); strong judgment on when and how to escalate. Diagnostics depth: confident with BMC/IPMI logs, Linux logs and CLI checks; structured root-cause analysis. Deployment experience: you've taken racks from delivery to production, with concrete examples to show for it. Vendor fluency: you've managed hardware vendors — RMAs, field replacements, escalations — to concrete outcomes. Impeccable safety and discipline: ESD/LOTO/PPE without exception; clean, labeled, auditable work. Communication & mentoring: clear status updates and handovers; able to coach engineers during live incidents with composure. Mobility: willing to visit our other sites in the Paris region as needed. Nice to have GPU-dense platform experience: NVIDIA H-series (H100/H200) or GB-series rack deployments. High-speed interconnects (InfiniBand/RoCE), RAID/storage (NVMe/SAS/SATA), vendor tooling (iDRAC/iLO/IPMI). Automation (Python/Bash) for ops tooling and reporting; ticketing (Jira/ServiceNow), inventory/RMA flows. Hardware qualification, burn-in or factory validation background. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks. For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page . Privacy Policy Your privacy matters to us. description: We are looking for a Propellant Quality Control Engineer to ensure the quality, consistency, and traceability of the materials and processes used to manufacture our solid propellants. Working closely with the Lead Propellant Manager, laboratory technicians, propulsion engineers, manufacturing, and suppliers, you will define and execute quality-control activities from incoming raw materials through to finished propellant. This is a hands-on role for someone who combines strong technical judgement with a disciplined approach to measurement, documentation, investigation, and process control. Your work will help ensure that propellant development and production remain safe, repeatable, and aligned with the required performance standards. About us We’re a Germany-based rocketry startup currently in stealth mode, scaling up rapidly to meet the demand for high-performance, reliable, and scalable solid propulsion technologies for space and defense applications. We are already launching suborbital and ballistic rockets on a regular basis, generating significant revenue and applying our knowledge toward the development of an orbital rocket. We are working hard to build something truly spectacular. To thrive here you will need to be comfortable working at pace, with the autonomy to make decisions and execute on them quickly. If you’re excited by hard technical challenges and want a role where you will make a real difference each day to the future of the company, we may be the place for you. At our company, job titles and career progression are earned, not determined by years of experience alone. They reflect the responsibility you take on and the dedication you bring to each project. If you’re ready to rise to the challenge, we’d love to hear from you. Key responsibilities Define and perform quality-control checks for raw materials, intermediate products, and finished propellant. Develop and maintain inspection plans, test methods, acceptance criteria, sampling requirements, and quality records. Review laboratory and production data to identify trends, variation, out-of-specification results, and emerging process issues. Lead or support investigations into non-conformances, deviations, material issues, and unexpected test results. Maintain clear traceability of materials, batches, samples, equipment, results, and technical decisions. Work with the Lead Propellant Manager and manufacturing teams to improve process capability, measurement quality, and production consistency. What we are looking for Experience in quality control, quality engineering, laboratory testing, or process control within a chemical, aerospace, manufacturing, or other regulated environment. A degree in chemical engineering, chemistry, materials science, mechanical engineering, or a related discipline. Strong understanding of measurement systems, test methods, sampling, data review, and technical documentation. Experience investigating non-conformances, identifying root causes, and implementing corrective actions. A methodical and detail-oriented approach to safety, traceability, data integrity, and compliance. Strong communication skills and the ability to work effectively with laboratory, engineering, manufacturing, quality, and supplier teams. Desirable experience Solid rocket propellants, energetic materials, Elastomers, polymers, binders, oxidisers, metallic fuels, or catalysts. Propellant or chemical-material characterisation, including thermal, mechanical, rheological, chemical, or burn-rate testing. Incoming-material inspection, supplier quality, batch release, certificate-of-analysis review, or material qualification. Statistical process control, measurement-system analysis, capability studies, trend analysis, or uncertainty assessment. Experience with hazardous chemicals, explosives, regulated materials, or formal laboratory and manufacturing quality systems. Python, MATLAB, laboratory information systems, electronic records, or other tools for quality and test-data analysis. Benefits and important information: We offer top-decile compensation packages, bonuses and meaningful equity, to attract exceptional aerospace talent. Every employee is awarded stock options in the company, you will directly benefit from your own hard work and success. Comprehensive relocation support including flights, shipping and visas. Lunch, dinner and drinks provided everyday Free access to shared company housing Please note, we are a fast paced, hyper-scaling startup. You will need to be comfortable working extended hours with high levels of autonomy, ownership, and flexibility, with contracts structured around a 48-hour working week. We are committed to building an equitable and inclusive workplace where everyone feels valued, has equal access to opportunity, and can thrive.
